clue.text: Where Annie Rooney was at home musically

definitions.text: Where Annie Rooney was at home musically

parts.words: Where Annie Rooney was at home musically
parts.note: Little Annie Rooney was a comic-strip orphan, and stage musicals about a parentless girl named Annie put her home in a children's institution

explanation.surface: A question about where a girl in a song lived, as if asking her address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At home' looks like a pointer to IN, but the whole clue is a description of a place where orphaned children live, the setting of musicals about Annie.
explanation.definitionFit: An institution housing children without parents is where a fictional orphan girl would be at home.

clue.text: Spaniard loses his head at cards

indicators.note: losing the head means the word for a Spanish man drops its first letter

parts.note: hombre is the Spanish word for a man, so it stands for a Spaniard

explanation.surface: A Spanish man is beheaded, or perhaps just loses his composure at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone losing his temper over a game; in fact HOMBRE loses its first letter H.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of an old three-handed Spanish trick-taking game played with a pack of forty.

clue.text: Growler uses phone at random

indicators.note: letters taken at random are jumbled, so the words phone and at are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dog or grumbler makes random phone calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growler' suggests a dog, but it is old slang for a four-wheeled horse cab, here matched with another horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A growler was a four-wheeled hackney cab, and this light open carriage is another horse-drawn vehicle.

clue.text: Boy goes to church in hail and falling snow

indicators.note: in places the boy-and-church string inside the word for hail

parts.note: ave is a Latin greeting, hail
Alan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad walks to church through hail and snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes to' is only a joining phrase between the boy and the church; 'in' does the containing, and 'hail' is the Latin greeting, not icy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sliding down a mountainside is snow falling in the most dramatic sense.

clue.text: Dryish wine peculiar to all domain

indicators.note: peculiar means odd, so the letters of to all domain are rearranged oddly

explanation.surface: A wine said to be unique to an entire estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peculiar to' reads as 'belonging only to', but 'peculiar' is the anagram signal on TO ALL DOMAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a medium-dry style of sherry from Montilla in Spain.

clue.text: Most of Vale is in decline

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the Welsh name is dropped

parts.note: Ebbw Vale is a town in South Wales, so Vale prompts its first word Ebbw

explanation.surface: A valley community is mostly in decline.
explanation.walkthrough: EBBW VALE is a former steel town in South Wales; 'Vale' calls up EBBW, and 'Most of' trims its W.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide's going out is a falling away, so the word means a state of decline.

clue.text: Little women's demo?

explanation.surface: A protest march by small women.
explanation.walkthrough: The four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women share this surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Meg, Jo, Beth and Amy are the family in Alcott's novel; a demo is a protest procession through the streets.

clue.text: Climbing range, I find Polynesian

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means reading upwards, so the word for range is turned backwards

parts.note: to range is to roam, wander widely

explanation.surface: A climber on a mountain range meets a Pacific islander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' looks like a mountain range but is a verb meaning wander; 'Climbing' turns it upwards in this down entry, and I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The indigenous people of New Zealand are Polynesians.

clue.text: The King is Emperor in Italy of course

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for a king
Otto was the name of several Holy Roman Emperors

explanation.surface: A king announces that the emperor is in Italy, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' seems to mean 'naturally', but it is the definition: a course of a meal in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice dish is a typical course in an Italian meal.

clue.text: Mad Mary had a daughter who lived in a tree

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters of Mary had a are scrambled

explanation.surface: Like a nursery rhyme gone wrong: crazy Mary has a daughter who lives in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme-like surface makes 'Mad Mary' a person; 'Mad' is the anagram signal on MARY HAD A, with D added.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a wood nymph's life was bound to the tree she inhabited.

clue.text: American law officer turns in desperado with a swagger

indicators.note: in places the turned lawyer inside the word for a desperado

parts.note: a bravo is a hired thug or desperado

indicators.note: turns means the abbreviation for the American lawyer is read backwards

parts.note: DA is a US District Attorney

explanation.surface: A US marshal turns up among outlaws, strutting confidently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperado' suggests a cowboy outlaw; it is the old word for a hired ruffian. 'Turns' flips the lawyer, 'in' contains, and 'with a' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Boastful show of daring is a kind of swaggering.

clue.text: Mature craft in the character of Ulysses

indicators.note: in places the craft inside the name of Joyce's hero

parts.note: Leopold Bloom is the hero of James Joyce's novel Ulysses
SS is a steamship, a vessel or craft

explanation.surface: Discussing a well-developed skill in the personality of Homer's hero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ulysses' suggests the Greek hero, but it is Joyce's novel, whose hero is Leopold BLOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into flower is to develop fully, to reach maturity.

clue.text: More than usually wide, for example

explanation.surface: Something unusually broad, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide, a ball bowled out of the batsman's reach, adds a run not scored off the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra means beyond the normal amount; a wide is one of cricket's sundries added to the total.

clue.text: Clumsy, though endowed with ducal twins

explanation.surface: An awkward person nonetheless blessed with twin dukes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dukes' is slang for fists, so a pair of ducal twins is two fists; the word also meant clumsy or heavy-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a pair of fists is literally the compound; ham-handed awkwardness is its older figurative sense.

clue.text: University seminar for religious teaching

parts.note: Oxford is the famous English university
a seminar is a discussion group

explanation.surface: A university study session about religion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oxford Group was Frank Buchman's 1920s-30s Christian movement, later Moral Re-Armament.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name of a Christian revivalist movement and its doctrine.

clue.text: Get bolt to slide easily

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a door bolt work smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a DIY tip, but there are three definitions: 'Get!' (clear off), bolt (flee), and slide easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Each sense is a verb: scram, flee, and move smoothly as a drawer does.

clue.text: Blood on the permanent way at Doncaster, perhaps?

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first word sits above the second

parts.note: blood means lineage or race
the permanent way is railway track

explanation.surface: Bloodshed on the railway line near Doncaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Doncaster is a northern English town with a famous horse-racing course, home of the St Leger.
explanation.definitionFit: The Doncaster course is an example of a circuit for horse racing.

clue.text: Warm room in fancy lace works

indicators.note: fancy means elaborately rearranged, so the word lace is jumbled

parts.note: a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A heated room in a fancy lace mill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy lace' reads as decorative lace; 'fancy' is the anagram signal giving CALE.
explanation.definitionFit: In a monastery this was the heated room where monks warmed themselves.

clue.text: Obligation for putting someone in prison

explanation.surface: Discussing the duty of sending someone to jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge binding oneself is an obligation; sending a person to jail or an asylum is the legal sense.

clue.text: Birmingham is after tin, possibly lead, for lampholder

indicators.note: is after means the Birmingham word comes last

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: possibly means the letters of lead may be rearranged

parts.note: Brum is the informal name for Birmingham

explanation.surface: Birmingham seeks tin, or maybe lead, to make a lamp stand.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUM is an everyday British nickname for Birmingham; 'possibly' scrambles LEAD to DELA.
explanation.definitionFit: A branched stand holding several candles or lights is a holder for lamps.

clue.text: Kind of navarin — out of this world for Buddhists

definitions.text: out of this world for Buddhists

indicators.note: kind of signals a variant form, so the letters of navarin are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lamb stew so good it is heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: A navarin is a French mutton stew; 'Kind of' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddhists seek release from the cycle of rebirth, a state beyond the world.

clue.text: Stinking fish thrown back

indicators.note: a fish thrown back is returned, so its name is reversed

parts.note: a dab is a flatfish

explanation.surface: An angler throws back a smelly fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrown back' reads as an angler's release; it turns DAB round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten or putrid food smells foul.

clue.text: Handkerchief with mono- gram perhaps

annotationWithheld.why: Handkerchief with monogram perhaps (7): BANDANA; no parse links 'monogram perhaps' to the letters and no blog or database gives one

clue.text: Flambeau's performing G.K. Chesterton's first sentimental ballad

parts.note: a flambeau is a flaming torch, and 's adds an S
on stage means performing

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the author's initials

explanation.surface: Flambeau, the reformed thief in G.K. Chesterton's Father Brown stories, puts on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Flambeau is Chesterton's thief-turned-detective, but here a flambeau is a torch; G is the first letter of G.K.
explanation.definitionFit: A song of unrequited love, sung by someone carrying a flame for another.

clue.text: Raise for one in a thousand, maybe

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for a multitude

parts.note: a host is a great number, a thousand for example
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Raising one in a thousand, a matter of odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in a thousand' reads as rarity; instead I goes in HOST, a large crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul something up is to lift it.

clue.text: Kind of tube near the heart

explanation.surface: A medical tube placed close to the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The rubber tube inside a tyre is so named; close to the centre or core means central, private.

clue.text: Elegant epitome of Biarritz youth

indicators.note: epitome suggests a compressed extract, so the letters are found within Biarritz youth

explanation.surface: A stylish young man of Biarritz, the very picture of chic.
explanation.walkthrough: The French resort Biarritz suggests glamour; the answer lies across its end and the start of 'youth'.
explanation.definitionFit: From a famous luxury hotel name, it means flashily smart and stylish.

clue.text: He goes back to type a tax return first

indicators.note: return means the tax word is turned backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: A man returns to typing his tax return first thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax return' reads as a form; 'return' turns VAT to TAV.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows traits of remote ancestors reverts to an earlier type.

clue.text: Face contraction in sound credit

indicators.note: in sound means the word for credit is heard, not spelt

parts.note: on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: A face twitches when hearing about credit.
explanation.walkthrough: TICK is British slang for credit ('buying on tick').
explanation.definitionFit: An involuntary twitch of facial muscles is a spasm of the face.

clue.text: Survive to end of the innings

explanation.surface: Lasting until the close of a cricket innings.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it describes the batsman dismissed last, the one whose dismissal ends the innings.
explanation.definitionFit: To live longer than something is to survive it; the final dismissal closes a cricket batting turn.

clue.text: Poisonous little snake — the Ark rejected it!

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word ark is reversed

explanation.surface: Noah turns away a venomous snake from the Ark.
explanation.walkthrough: The Noah picture hides the device: 'rejected' turns ARK into KRA.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a highly venomous banded snake of South Asia.

clue.text: This can have an attraction, like hair

explanation.surface: Something both attractive and hairlike.
explanation.walkthrough: Capillary attraction draws liquid up narrow tubes; the word comes from Latin capillus, hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Capillary action draws liquids up fine tubes; the adjective means hairlike, as fine blood vessels are.
